newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch money rates seen locked in tight range.
newsitem.headline: Dutch money rates seen locked in tight range.

text.p: Dutch money market rates were unaffected by the stronger than expected German M3 data earlier on Thursday and dealers said rates were likely to remain stable for some more time.
The guilder was stronger as a result of increasing trust in the Dutch economy, with the currency trading at 112.26 per 100 marks versus 112.30 yesterday.
The German Q4 GDP figure, also announced earlier, was unchanged from the previous quarter, the Bundesbank said.
January M3 grew an annualised 8.6 percent versus 7.9 percent in December, while analysts had expected a drop to 6.0 percent.
"Rates are likely to stay unchanged for some more months," said one dealer, adding that the market would be happy with any change. "Movements trigger business," he said.
Some business was done in the shorter end of the curve.
"The Dutch government was searching for call money to pay out salaries," said one dealer. But the amount was not great, as call money rates were lingering near yesterday's level at 2.87 percent bid.
Dealers expect no change in the Dutch special advances rate when the central bank sets a new pact at 1500 GMT, since Germany left its official rates and the repo unchanged.
Three-month deposits were trading at an unchanged 2.92 percent.
Six-month and one-year deposits rose fractionally as the bond market was a little lower today.
One-year deposits were up two basis points at 3.10 percent bid.
